column3: §FILM_FACT sheets · the 9 raw sheets open (no Arrange play)
column4: F: I drew this shed in BricsCAD. What does it make of it?
column5: F: I drew this shed in BricsCAD. What does the Modeller make of it? | M: It opens your {sheets} sheets exactly as they are. Nothing in your files is changed. First it reads what they say, then it lists what they do not.

column3: §FILM_FACT open_yellow / g_units / g_view / g_name / open_n · the grouped list
column4: M: {open_yellow} values, in three groups: units, view, name.
column5: F: What is this list? | M: Everything your sheets do not state outright, grouped. {open_yellow} values: the units on {g_units} sheets, which view each one is on {g_view}, and the name on {g_name}. Yellow means it was read from a text on the sheet. You only confirm it.

column3: §FILM_FACT g_grid / g_level / g_ground · after the three groups are ticked
column4: M: One tick per group. Next: {g_grid} grid rows.
column5: F: And I just tick them? | M: One group at a time. Each tick opens the next questions: {g_grid} grid lines read from your dimension ticks, {g_level} plan levels, and {g_ground} ground lines. Orange means inferred, not read.

column3: §FILM_FACT rings / boxed_open / box_open_word · the Sheet view of the floor plan
column4: M: Your floor plan, full frame. {rings} rings: the grid, never named.
column5: M: This is the Sheet view: your floor plan, full frame, as you drew it. | F: What are the rings? | M: {rings} grid lines the drawing never names. Each ring sits where the value was read, at a grid bubble. The box lists what is stated, and the one still open: {box_open_word}.

column3: DXF2BIMGuide "Drawing in BricsCAD" (grid lines row) · the grid group ticked
column4: F: Could I have drawn it so it never asks?
column5: F: Could I have drawn it so it never has to ask? | M: Yes. Draw each grid line as a line on a grid layer, with its label at its end. Then every line is read, not inferred. Here, I tick the grid group instead.

column3: §FILM_FACT positional · the Sheet view again
column4: M: The {positional} rings are now markings, on the sheet.
column5: M: Back on the sheet, the {positional} rings are now markings, written where they were read. | F: Written where, exactly? | M: Into copies of your DXF, on a layer of their own. Your originals stay as they were.

column3: §FILM_FACT after_accept_n · the rest of the list accepted
column4: M: The rest, accepted in one click: {after_accept_n} left.
column5: M: The rest of the list, accepted in one click. | F: Is it ready to convert? | M: Not yet. {after_accept_n} things still block it, and only a person can state them.

column3: §FILM_FACT set_name · the set name typed
column4: M: The set's name: one word, {set_name}.
column5: F: What can it not read at all? | M: The name of the set. No drawing states it. One word, {set_name}, typed once for every sheet.

column3: §FILM_FACT heights_typed · the second heights typed
column4: M: {heights_typed} heights, one per elevation.
column5: M: Each elevation and section needs a second height to stand up straight. {heights_typed} heights, one per sheet.

column3: §FILM_FACT layers_stated · the layer types chosen (the CLI-marked set's @LAYER: Col=column, Fo=footing / bar, Win=elevdoor)
column4: M: {layers_stated} short layer names, each given a meaning.
column5: F: And my short layer names? | M: Each one is given its meaning: Col is a column. Fo is a footing on one sheet and a bar on another, so it is answered per sheet. {layers_stated} answers in all.

column3: §FILM_FACT bodyz_typed / bodies_before_exclude / bodies_after_exclude · body heights + the exclude
column4: M: {bodies_before_exclude} bodies become {bodies_after_exclude}.
column5: M: Two body heights no elevation shows, and one stray area left out of the beam plan: {bodies_before_exclude} bodies become {bodies_after_exclude}.

column3: §FILM_FACT building_type / saved_files / raw_unchanged · the type set, Save
column4: M: Farming Shed. Then {saved_files} marked copies saved.
column5: F: Farming Shed? | M: The building type. It decides what you may do with it later, like adding a bay. Then Save: {saved_files} marked copies, as new files. Your originals are untouched.

column3: §FILM_FACT converted / n_column / n_beam / n_wall / n_member / n_plate / n_door / door_gap_cuts · Convert
column4: M: {converted} bodies, built from your nine sheets.
column5: M: Convert. {converted} bodies: {n_column} columns, {n_beam} beams, {n_wall} walls, {n_member} members and {n_plate} roof sheets. | F: And the doors? | M: {n_door} doors. The double door now sits in its wall, in {door_gap_cuts} openings.

column3: §FILM_FACT wall_len / moved_cm · the typed move
column4: M: One wall, {wall_len} metres. Ten centimetres: it moves {moved_cm}.
column5: F: Can I change it, then? | M: In small steps. One wall, {wall_len} metres long. Type a step of ten centimetres and press an arrow: it moves {moved_cm} centimetres.

column3: §FILM_FACT len_before / len_after · the typed stretch
column4: M: Five percent longer: {len_before} becomes {len_after}.
column5: M: Now stretch it by five percent: {len_before} metres becomes {len_after}.

column3: §FILM_FACT undo_back_m / redo_back_m · Ctrl+Z twice, Ctrl+Y twice
column4: F: And if I change my mind?
column5: F: And if I change my mind? | M: Control Z, twice: the wall is back exactly where it was. Control Y brings both steps back.

column3: §FILM_FACT bay_hinge / bay_copies / bay_moved / bay_stretched / bay_riders · Add a bay
column4: M: One more bay: {bay_copies} parts copied, {bay_stretched} stretched.
column5: M: Farm sheds grow by whole bays. Add a bay at grid line {bay_hinge}: {bay_copies} parts copied, {bay_moved} moved one bay on, {bay_stretched} long members stretched. | F: And the double door? | M: It rides its wall: {bay_riders} hosted parts.

column3: §FILM_FACT bay_cur / bay_total / bay_added / bay_changed / bay_gate_words · the cost + the gate
column4: F: What does that cost?
column5: F: What does that cost? | M: {bay_total} {bay_cur} more: {bay_added} for the new parts, {bay_changed} for the longer ones. And the conformity check is {bay_gate_words}.

column3: §FILM_FACT svg_saved · the marked sheet saved as SVG
column4: M: Your floor plan, with its markings, saved as SVG.
column5: M: Back to your floor plan, now with its markings. Save it as SVG, or print it, for the next person who opens the set.

column3: DXF2BIMGuide "## Prior art" (§FILM_FACT prior_art_text) · the prior-art card
column4: F: Has nobody done this before?
column5: F: Has nobody done this before? | M: Other tools detect walls, doors and windows with default parameters, and ask a subscription. Here the gaps are stated, every body keeps where it came from, and you are asked only for the facts in the yellow list. No head-to-head test has been run.
